fatal_errors: The proposed TiC-CaF2-graphite material does not reconstruct the target CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite or the Mo-content intervention.
No evidence supports the selected phase fractions, processing conditions, or quantitative friction and wear improvements.
Graphite oxidation and tribofilm stability in air up to 800 °C are not addressed, undermining the claimed wide-temperature lubrication mechanism.
Critical test parameters—including atmosphere, counterface, sliding distance, and specimen preparation—are omitted.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general goal of wide-temperature self-lubrication and supplies a clear unreinforced-TiC baseline plus a falsifiable tribology test. However, it is scientifically disconnected from the target intervention, which varies Mo in an HEA composite and relies on Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, and high-temperature NiO/silver-molybdate glaze formation. The proposed CaF2/graphite mechanism is only asserted, and the predicted 30% friction and 50% wear reductions are arbitrary without cited or generated evidence. Its broad 200–800 °C scope overlaps the target range, but the loads and speeds differ and essential environmental details are absent. Because graphite may oxidize substantially at elevated temperature in air, the claimed continuous film requires direct validation; absent such evidence, this is an unsupported alternative rather than a plausible reconstruction.
